Latest To-Do List Item: Find Replacement for Microsoft To Do

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news.
  • We’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired.
  • Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news. One of the best free options for organizing your work and home life is reaching the end of its life. Microsoft looks to retire its To Do app at the end of June 2027.

We’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired. But several Microsoft-watching websites this week spotted a blog post from the organization recommending owners switch to its Planner app.

Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring. For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.

Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. This includes To Do on the web, Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android, for both work or school accounts and personal Microsoft accounts.

In a recent development, the underlying To Do service, APIs, and related synchronization support will retire on separate, later timelines. We’ll communicate those dates and any required preparation separately.

Sources indicate that but there’s a massive catch for Microsoft customers who are on 365 Personal or 365 Family plans: Planner will not be available to them. That means Microsoft is telling To Do consumers on those accounts to find a comparable app elsewhere if they’re not on a business account that includes Planner.

The change was also mentioned in a separate Microsoft post about unified tasks and aims for Copilot and Microsoft 365 from Microsoft product manager Ashna Patel.

In a statement provided to CNET, Howard Crow, director of product, agents and AI at Microsoft, mentioned the change consolidates task management across Microsoft 365. “We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare,” Crow said.

Crow noted the tech giant will share more information about the transition in the coming months.

According to recent reports, while the end of June 2027 may sound like a very long time from now, the path Microsoft has offered for To Do consumers is not a great one if you want to take action now. There’s no built-in export feature in the app, though in the blog post, Microsoft promises, “Microsoft will provide a way to export your To Do data before the apps retire. We’ll revision this article with instructions, supported data, requirements, and limitations when those details are finalized.”.

Industry observers note that already, there are some pretty severe limitations even for those on Microsoft plans that support Planner: Existing To Do list items won’t work after that June deadline. “After that date, you will no longer be able to view or manage them in Planner,” the post noted.

In the meantime, you can shop around for alternate apps, some free, including Google Keep, ToDoist and Notion.

Industry observers note that to Do users, myself included, are not happy. As Windows Latest reported, comments in response to Microsoft’s decision included, “Do you actually hate your users?”.

According to recent reports, if this were simply a case of Microsoft creating software people didn’t like and then abandoning it, that would be one thing. But the To Do retirement is especially painful for those of us who were forced to move to Microsoft’s app a few years after it purchased Wunderlist.

Wunderlist was a German app that launched in 2011 and swiftly became popular for its slick interface, easy-to-update task lists and its availability across web, desktop and mobile platforms. Microsoft absorbed some of Wunderlist into To Do and killed the original app in 2020 without ever offering all of the features that made Wunderlist great.

According to recent reports, as someone who used Wunderlist for years and has been using To Do, I can tell you that while To Do has been essential in my work and personal life, it never became as intuitive to use as Wunderlist. It never handled predictive task creation as well as Wunderlist did (such as understanding as you typed the date of a task or if it was repeating). It lacked features for sharing lists or collaborating on them, and simply didn’t look as stylish. As far as aesthetics, the best thing Microsoft did with To Do was add a Dark Mode.

Sources indicate that wunderlist was a joy to use. To Do always felt like the knockoff diet version of it and never quite as good.

After several years, I simply gave up on the idea that Microsoft would improve the app or add any fresh features, but kept using it out of necessity given the lack of a built-in export option.

Industry observers note that the death announcement is not surprising. Just sad.

RIP To Do, but really RIP to the last remnants of Wunderlist.

    Sources indicate that jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that the Vera Rubin architecture can deliver up to 30 times more performance than Nvidia's previous Blackwell Ultra architecture, which could translate to a 97% reduction in inference token costs. Inference tokens are the text, images, or computer code generated by an AI model in response to a prompt, so in simple terms, Vera Rubin could dramatically lower the cost of running AI software.

    Lower costs have the potential to increase AI adoption while also making data center operators more profitable -- two things that could significantly increase demand for Nvidia's chips over time.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, who is now expected to return to her role as chief financial officer, recently noted Vera Rubin generated almost $20 billion in sales during Nvidia's fiscal 2027 third quarter (ended Oct. 25), making this the fastest product ramp-up in the firm's history.

    I think that forecast is all the more likely to come to fruition with Huang back at the helm, so it could set the stage for a year of great returns in 2027 -- and investors can buy Nvidia stock at what I believe to be a bargain valuation right now.     We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (933 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, five years ago, NASA released its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed.
    • It has been revealed that the ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere.
    • At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, five years ago, NASA released its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed. The mission was a success, making Dimorphos the first celestial object whose orbit was moved by humans. And now, the European Space Agency has published images showing the damage the mission caused to the asteroid.

    It has been revealed that the ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere. The images shown during the livestream were captured by the ESA’s Hera, which was debuted in October 2024 and spent two years in deep space with its two CubeSats to measure, map, probe and eventually land on the asteroid.

    At the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth. But they were unable to get a good enough view to see how much damage it did to the asteroid or any other potential changes that occurred.

    In a recent development, this means that researchers had to estimate the damage until Hera showed scientists exactly what happened. Spoiler: All of those estimates were incorrect, and by a wide margin.

    Recent findings suggest that hera revealed the damage was vastly more significant than originally thought. Scientists believed the impact would generate a 20-meter crater; Hera found that almost the entire end of the asteroid had been blown off, resulting in a crater the size of a football stadium and as wide as Dimorphos itself. This is visible in the above image — as you can see, Dimorphos used to be roughly the shape of an egg. Now, it’s the shape of a deviled egg or a kidney bean, depending on which angle you view it from.

    Recent findings suggest that the ESA’s Hera team discovered another neat effect of the impact: Before DART crashed into the asteroid, it was tidally locked to Didymos, much like the moon is to Earth. Scientists expected it to stay that way after the impact, but the images from Hera confirmed that Dimorphos now tumbles randomly, which none of the researchers had on their bingo card.

    “Before the DART impact, Dimorphos has always shown its same face to Didymos,” said ESA Hera Mission Specialist Michael Kueppers during the presentation. “And this is what we see now. You can see it looks for a few seconds in the video like regular rotation, but it’s spinning around completely crazy.”.

    ESA mission manager Ian Carnelli said this surprise was great news because it’ll allow Hera to view Dimorphos on all of its sides, which would have been challenging if it were still tidally locked to Didymos.

    The ESA concluded the stream with one final surprise. According to Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, the Hera team told engineers that it was entirely safe to go to Dimorphos because all the debris would be ejected from the DART impact, with the remaining bits reabsorbed by Didymos and Dimorphos before Hera arrived.

    But there is actually quite a lot of debris around the two asteroids. Kueppers claims they’ve identified over 100 boulders so far, marked as white dots in the image above. Despite being completely wrong about the debris field, the Hera team was in good spirits since this means there are more things for the team to study.

    Sources indicate that kueppers claims scientists are “always happy” either way because when they predict something correctly, they get awarded, and when they predict something wrong, they have a challenge to solve. “The problem is for the engineers,” he mentioned.

    The three discoveries were made just 20 days into Hera’s mission, which is slated to last six months. The Hera team mentioned more images and discoveries are coming in the next half year.

    The point of the DART mission was to see whether humans could deal with a potentially dangerous asteroid by ramming into it or destroying it, as is often seen in Hollywood films like Deep Impact and Armageddon. NASA even frames it as a “planetary defense test.”.

    Industry observers note that the mission was considered an overwhelming success. NASA was hoping to shorten the orbit of Dimorphos by at least 73 seconds, with the most optimal guess being approximately 10 minutes. The orbit was shortened by 33 minutes and 15 seconds. It was such a large discrepancy that scientists studied it and determined that the large amount of debris created extra recoil that amplified the push.

    It has been revealed that the change in orbit around Didymos also changed the orbit of both asteroids around the sun by about 11.7 microns per second. This doesn’t seem significant, but it adds up to about 1 kilometer every 2.7 years. This is enough to steer potential city-killer asteroids away from Earth’s orbit, given enough time and a significant enough battering ram.

    Sources indicate that hera’s findings also show the impact was much more devastating than scientists first thought. This provides even more data for NASA and the ESA to work through to strategy for such an event if it ever happens.

    “As new data come in each day, astronomers will be able to better assess whether, and how, a mission like DART could be used in the future to help protect Earth from a collision with an asteroid if we ever discover one headed our way,” mentioned Lori Glaze, director of NASA’s Planetary Science Division, in a statement from 2022.

    Time Is Running Out for Apple’s iPhone Settlement. How to File a Claim Before Dec. 21

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec.
    • According to recent reports, the class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet.
    • The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec. 21, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

    According to recent reports, the class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

    The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

    Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

    Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the new devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

    Industry observers note that if you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

    “Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our people,” an Apple spokesperson said in an earlier statement to CNET.

    It has been revealed that the court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

    Industry observers note that “False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” remarked Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

    Apple lit up its flagship New York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

    According to recent reports, as of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the firm Verita directing them to the website.

    Recent findings suggest that the claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

    If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:.

    The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

    It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

    Sources indicate that when Apple advertised its new iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

    According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”.

    It has been revealed that some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

    Sources indicate that according to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

    After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

    On Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

    Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

    What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • Recent findings suggest that A visual exterior inspection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    Recent findings suggest that A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    Sources indicate that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any concerns are documented.

    According to recent reports, A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    Recent findings suggest that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic problems that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Industry observers note that inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    Detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    It has been revealed that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    It has been revealed that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Reddit is an online forum where consumers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several consumers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo.
    • Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter.
    • According to recent reports, the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo. Notice the lights on the tree, compared to the green hue of the street lighting and blue and pink tones in the sky.

    Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter. The winter solstice is on Dec. 21, when we’ll experience Earth’s shortest, darkest day.

    According to recent reports, the winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them. The most common definition, and the one you’re most likely familiar with, is that it denotes the shortest day and longest night of the year on Earth. These times vary depending on your location on the globe, but the further north you live, the less sunlight you’ll get. In the tropics, they’ll get about 12 hours of sunlight. In Sweden, it’ll be closer to 6 hours. In Svalbard, there isn’t any.

    Industry observers note that the reason this occurs is due to the second definition of the winter solstice: During this time, the North Pole is tilted as far away from the sun as it can get. According to The Farmer’s Almanac, the moment at which the Earth’s axis is physically tilted as much as it can be is at 3:50 p.m. ET on Monday, Dec. 21. After that moment, the process will begin to reverse until the South Pole takes its turn during the summer solstice. At that point, the North Pole will be at its closest tilt to the sun, giving us the longest day and shortest night of the year for the Northern Hemisphere.

    In a recent development, sunset will occur at its earliest time on Dec. 21.

    It has been revealed that it’ll vary by location. The southern US will have the most sunlight, with Florida getting a little over 10 hours during the winter solstice. The Midwest and Great Lakes portion of the country will get roughly nine hours. The Pacific Northwest can expect a little less than nine hours. Southern Alaska will get about six hours, and the northern areas of Alaska will see around three hours.

    If you want to see how your area will fare, Time and Date has a sunrise and sunset tool you can use. Input your zip code into the search bar, and you’ll be able to see your sunrise and sunset times.

    The city of Utqiaġvik, Alaska, will have it worse than most in the US: It won’t get any sun at all. The sun won’t rise there again until late January. We hope the people living there packed their vitamin D supplements.

    Sources indicate that the autumn equinox was just a couple of months ago, so you may be curious about the differences. A solstice occurs when the Earth’s poles are tilted as far away from the sun as they’ll be over the course of one year, which is also one orbit around the sun. The equinoxes take place at the halfway points between each solstice. The autumn equinox takes place in September between the summer and winter solstices, while the spring equinox takes place in March between the winter and summer.

    During an equinox, the poles are minimally tilted, and the days are as even as they can be. This also has a couple of other interesting side effects: The sun is pointed directly at the equator during an equinox, and the sun will rise and set directly east and west, respectively.

    In a recent development, humans use the solstices and equinoxes to mark the change of the seasons. There are two equinoxes and two solstices, which mark the start and end dates for Earth’s four seasons.

    Decorating with evergreen trees, like with a wreath, is what they used to do to celebrate the winter solstice.

    Recent findings suggest that while the solstice is close to the holidays, celebrations for the winter solstice have been around for significantly longer, and some winter solstice traditions have become Christmas traditions as well. One of the most historically famous winter solstice celebrations is Yule, a winter festival originating thousands of years ago among the ancient Norse. It became commonly celebrated in Europe and involved bonfires and massive feasts. Yule celebrations also included decorating with evergreen tree decorations, like holly and ivy.

    If these sound familiar, it’s because Christmas co-opted many of those traditions centuries ago, and the two traditions have kind of merged into a single seasonal holiday. The terms Yule and Christmas are often used interchangeably these days in many cultures.

    According to recent reports, so if you want to celebrate the winter solstice, just do all of the stuff you would normally do for the holidays. Burn a Yule log, decorate a tree, eat a significant feast with your family and hang up mistletoe and wreaths — those are all hat tips to traditional winter solstice celebrations.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Elon Musk's social network X just got a fresh feature it never had under previous ownership.

    It has been revealed that that would be parental controls for teen people, to be exact. In a latest post from the official Safety account on X, the organization announced it has implemented parental controls for users aged 13 to 17. The way it works is that an account run by a parent or guardian establishes a supervisory link to the account run by a teen, which gives the parent or guardian access to a bunch of monitoring and safety features the site didn't have before.

    These features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require new followers to be approved by the parent or guardian. Recommendations on the For You feed can be limited to accounts the teen already follows, while parents can mute specific words, control who can send direct messages, and see who the teens have chatted with in DMs without seeing the messages themselves.

    The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

    Industry observers note that as X noted, this only starts when both parties in the equation consent to it, so a teen cannot have their account limited against their will. Theoretically, anyway. A parent account can supervise as many as five teen accounts, but a teen account can only be linked to one parent account.

    This is interesting because it's an acknowledgment by X that some teenagers do use the platform, but even in the Safety account's post, the company is clear that X is "not designed for or promoted to children." Indeed, one could argue that teen owners should stay far away from a service that has become home to hate speech, widespread misinformation, and a Grok AI chatbot that has gotten up to plenty of unsavory business since it was introduced.

    But if teens are going to use X, at least these features exist now.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.
    • The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase concerns and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.
    • The complaint also alleges problems with the company’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.

    The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase concerns and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

    The complaint also alleges problems with the company’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.

    “The firm misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews,” Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, stated in a statement on Tuesday.

    Shein has ballooned over the past decade into the ultra-fast-fashion brand we know today, thanks in large part to the impact influencers have had on social media, posting videos trying on clothing supplied by the company.

    In a recent development, in 2026, the company is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC. That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.

    Recent findings suggest that this isn’t the first time Shein has faced negative scrutiny. Over the years, the company has faced allegations of numerous workers’ rights violations and is the largest polluter in the fast-fashion industry.

    According to Yale Climate Connections, the tech giant emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023. Comparatively speaking, that’s more than the pollution output of four coal power plants. Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

    It has been revealed that the $100 million will be used to compensate customers. And according to the FTC’s proposed order, the organization, which earned roughly $50 billion in revenue in 2025, will not be able to continue advertising inaccurate shipping and delivery times; negative reviews will no longer be hidden; and its customer service offering will be bolstered.

    “The agreement does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices,” a Shein spokesperson told CNET.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1060 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    In a recent development, one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a newly introduced region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    It has been revealed that repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

    In a recent development, if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    It has been revealed that for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    It has been revealed that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    Sources indicate that you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    In a recent development, keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    According to recent reports, here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between New York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Sources indicate that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan.     If an AI Bubble Bursts, This Is the Only Tech Stock I Want to Own

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If construction activity at every half-built AI data center in America went quiet, which tech giant would feel it least?
    • The mood on Wall Street has swung hard.
    • To be clear: If the AI boom keeps roaring, there will be faster growers in big tech than Apple.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:46AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

    If construction activity at every half-built AI data center in America went quiet, which tech giant would feel it least? I've chewed on that question a lot as tech stock prices have whipsawed this fall, and my answer keeps coming back to one name: Apple (AAPL +0.43%).

    The mood on Wall Street has swung hard. A broad tech sell-off pushed all three major indexes into correction territory, and the leadership whirlwind at Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%), which ended with its board reinstating CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, showed how much of the market now hangs on one AI story. Apple, meanwhile, still trades within a few percentage points of its 52-week high.

    To be clear: If the AI boom keeps roaring, there will be faster growers in big tech than Apple. This is about the one tech stock I'd want to hold if it doesn't.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that the AI race has turned Apple's megacap peers into construction companies. Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%) is on course to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital expenditures this year, mostly on AI, and it posted negative free cash flow last quarter. So did Meta Platforms (META +3.40%).

    Apple spent about $9 billion on property and equipment in its entire fiscal 2026 — that’s less than it laid out the year before. Instead of building data centers and developing new foundation AI models, the iPhone maker rents what it needs. It struck a deal to base its next foundation models on Google's Gemini after deciding "Google's AI technology provides the most capable foundation." That's the honest weak spot. Apple was late to the generative AI party, the debut of its upgraded Siri slipped by a full year, and it leaned on a rival to catch up.

    It has been revealed that but being late can mean being cheaper. Much of Apple's AI runs on the device itself.

    "On device -- it's very, very efficient. No real costs associated with that," CFO Kevan Parekh mentioned on the November earnings call. Businesses are noticing, too. Gap (GAP +2.52%) is running its AI loss-prevention models on Mac Minis across hundreds of stores, "eliminating cloud token costs," Parekh said. CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September, put it simply: "Apple devices, we think, are the best places to use all forms of AI.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Apple's real defense is the 2.5 billion active devices in people's pockets and on their desks.

    "Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high," Parekh said. Those customers carry more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions, and Apple’s services segment revenue hit a record last quarter with a 76% gross margin. Ternus calls the iPhone an "intelligent personal hub," noting that "so much of your personal data is on your iPhone.".

    Industry observers note that services isn't bulletproof, though. Parekh flagged headwinds from third-party licensing, softer mobile gaming, and an unfavorable U.S. court ruling on App Store payment links.

    Then there's the cash. Apple ended the quarter with $137 billion in cash and securities on its books against $80 billion in debt, and it returned $28 billion to shareholders, including $24 billion in stock buybacks. The company’s approach, Parekh said, is to "invest in our business and return excess cash to shareholders.".

    Here's the twist I find most interesting: The AI infrastructure build-out is hurting Apple right now because data centers are gobbling up so many memory chips.

    "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," Ternus said, adding that "we see the pricing for memory purchases continuing to increase." Apple expects lower gross margins this quarter, primarily due to memory costs, and has already raised prices on iPhones, Macs, and iPads to reflect its higher costs.

    None of that makes the stock cheap. Trading at about 39 times earnings, Apple carries a premium P/E ratio, and during real market panics, pricey stocks get sold along with everything else. Apple stock could still fall if an AI bubble bursts. The case I’m making is that its business wouldn't.

    When I picture the AI party ending, I see builders writing down the value of their data centers and one manufacturer with 2.5 billion customers paying less for memory and renting AI from whichever infrastructure players survive. That's the side of the table I'd want to be sitting on.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • According to recent reports, two big-name tech investors have landed in different places on Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -1.75%).
    • As of this writing, the stock trades near $376, off about 42% over seven weeks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:53AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    According to recent reports, two big-name tech investors have landed in different places on Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -1.75%). Cathie Wood's Ark Invest added almost 50,000 shares of the chipmaker on Friday, Nov. 20, when the stock dropped 13%. Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management, though, owned no AMD shares at all at the end of September, according to its newest quarterly filing.

    The split follows a steep slide. AMD's record close was on Oct. 6, at $649.42. As of this writing, the stock trades near $376, off about 42% over seven weeks.

    According to recent reports, and in the third quarter, both investors sold. Only Wood has been reported buying back in since.

    Cathie Wood. Image source: Getty Images.

    In a recent development, coatue's 13F filings (the quarterly forms big money managers use to disclose their U.S.-listed stock holdings) show a fund that has exited AMD twice in 2026. It ended 2025 with around 1.24 million AMD shares, a stake then worth $265 million, and it ended March with none.

    Industry observers note that that first exit looks badly timed now. The growth stock closed the first quarter at around $203 and almost tripled by the end of June. Even after this fall's sell-off, the stock trades well above its highest first-quarter close of about $260.

    Coatue did buy back in during that climb, ending June with about 96,000 shares worth about $56 million. But that was a small stake, roughly 0.1% of the $48.6 billion in holdings the filing demonstrated.

    And by Sept. 30, the position was gone again. AMD closed the third quarter at about $612, so the second exit has aged well, with shares off about 39% since.

    A 13F indicates holdings, not reasons. But Coatue's filing doesn't look like a pullback from chips. As of Sept. 30, the fund had over $3 billion each in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Micron Technology, and Lam Research. Laffont still seems to be betting massive on the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. AMD just wasn't part of it when the quarter ended.

    Ark has traded AMD in both directions this year. After buying shares in January and February, its funds sold AMD on dozens of days from late March to late October while the stock rose. The largest sale was on Sept. 29, around a week before the record close, when Ark sold 181,767 shares worth about $110 million.

    Then the buying began again. Ark picked up almost 49,000 shares on Nov. 5, a day AMD dropped 17%, and 49,745 more on Nov. 20.

    In a recent development, valued at those days' closes, the two purchases came to about $41 million. Together, they equal a bit over half the shares Ark sold on Sept. 29 alone, bought back at closing prices 30% to 33% lower.

    AMD is now around 2% of the flagship ARK Innovation ETF, a far bigger part of the fund than the stake Coatue reported in June.

    In a recent development, the case for Wood's buy depends on how fast AMD's business is growing. Its data center segment, home to the tech giant's Instinct AI chips and EPYC server processors, had record sales of $8.5 billion in the third quarter. Growth from the previous quarter has picked up all year, from around 7% in Q1 to 16% in Q2 and then 27% in Q3. Management expects about 50% sequential growth for the segment in the fourth quarter. And for 2027, it expects total revenue to climb over 80%, with data center making up more than 80% of sales.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    "It is true that demand is higher than supply," CEO Lisa Su stated during AMD's third-quarter earnings call.

    According to recent reports, demand that tops supply is promising, but it also means AMD's outlook relies on getting enough parts to make all those chips. Preparing for that growth is a drag on cash flow. Inventory climbed around $3 billion from the second quarter to $11.5 billion, and free cash flow dropped 64% year over year to $554 million.

    Sources indicate that the price, meanwhile, has come down a long way. Measured against analysts' average 2027 estimate of around $17.60 per share, AMD's third-quarter close near $612 was almost 35 times earnings. The current price of $376 works out to about 21 times earnings on the same estimate.

    It has been revealed that ark's September sale and Laffont's second exit both look well timed so far. But for someone buying now, I think Wood is right. I'd consider buying AMD shares at this price, and I'd only rethink that if supply complications put its 2027 outlook out of reach.

    • Like many IPO stocks, Anthropic enjoyed a first-day pop, sending the shares to $97.17 at the close.
    • But investing in mega-IPOs like Anthropic after their debut isn't always a great decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:04AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) just set a record for the largest amount of capital raised in an IPO. The AI lab's offering raised $81 billion, topping the $75 billion raised by Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%) earlier this year. Anthropic also took in about $26 billion in cash from a separate private placement with several big tech companies.

    Like many IPO stocks, Anthropic enjoyed a first-day pop, sending the shares to $97.17 at the close. That could leave many investors with FOMO, as the AI lab looks to inject upcoming life into AI stocks that have been sluggish over the last few weeks.

    But investing in mega-IPOs like Anthropic after their debut isn't always a great decision. Here's what history says about buying into substantial IPOs.

    Recent findings suggest that IPO stocks don't have a great track record. Investors often end up losing money on their investments after three years. Indeed, 60% of all IPOs between 1975 and 2021 ended with prices below their first-day close after three years of trading publicly.

    Sources indicate that the odds are much better for bigger companies. Companies with at least $1 billion in sales (adjusted for inflation) saw an average three-year buy-and-hold return of 32.4% from their first-day closing price, well above the 17.8% average for IPOs with less than $1 billion in trailing-12-month sales. That mentioned, the average mega-IPO still produces an average return below the rest of the market in its first three years of trading.

    Sources indicate that recent history hasn't been too kind either. SpaceX and SK Hynix (SKHY -0.75%) had two of the largest IPOs in history this year. As mentioned, SpaceX raised $75 billion when it went public in June. While SK Hynix traded on the Korean stock exchange, its Nasdaq debut raised an additional $26.5 billion by making it easier for American investors to buy the stock. Today, both stocks trade below their first-day closing price.

    In a recent development, the table includes the 10 largest IPOs on U.S. stock exchanges of the last 15 years:.

    *Less than one year since IPO, returns are to date.Data source: Renaissance Capital and Google Finance.

    As you can see, the track record isn't great for the biggest U.S. IPOs, which tend to generate significant media attention and investor buzz. As such, the stocks are priced rather than valued, and with so much excitement about the companies, that excitement can push prices well above fair value.

    Sources indicate that while history isn't kind to the biggest IPOs, investors need to evaluate stocks on a case-by-case basis. Anthropic's valuation was previously floated at around $2 trillion before AI stocks began facing selling pressure amid financing concerns and potential regulatory hurdles following the midterm elections. At a fully diluted market cap of around $1.8 trillion after its first day of trading, Anthropic hasn't been immune to those pressures.

    Sources indicate that but Anthropic is arguably well positioned to handle financing challenges. It now holds $232 billion in cash and equivalents on its balance sheet. What's more, it has financing in place using convertible note purchase agreements with multiple strategic partners totaling $77 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    That remarked, Anthropic will have to continue growing revenue at an extremely rapid pace over the next five to 10 years while demonstrating considerable operating leverage. That's definitely possible based on its recent results, but there are significant risks in forecasting the future of a rapidly evolving industry. That means Anthropic shares are likely to be highly volatile in the near term, which may present a better buying opportunity than right after its IPO.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

    Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    The amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

    In a recent development, my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

    Recent findings suggest that here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Sources indicate that mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

    Recent findings suggest that strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

    Sources indicate that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Markets are at the moment anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

    But back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    In a recent development, securitize reinforced "certain areas of the tech giant like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo mentioned. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    According to recent reports, securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo remarked.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    3 Investing Moves All Investors Should Make Right Now if a Bear Market Is Coming

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that nobody can predict exactly when the next bear market will hit, but that doesn't mean investors should wait to prepare for it.
    • To that end, here are three investing moves to help protect portfolios today.
    • Cash is often put to use during bull markets because it doesn't offer the same excitement as fast-growing stocks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Orford – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:19AM EST.

    Industry observers note that nobody can predict exactly when the next bear market will hit, but that doesn't mean investors should wait to prepare for it. After all, if market volatility continues to rise, having the right strategy can make a substantial difference.

    To that end, here are three investing moves to help protect portfolios today.

    Cash is often put to use during bull markets because it doesn't offer the same excitement as fast-growing stocks. But when markets become volatile, having some extra cash on the side can be a huge advantage.

    For one, cash can help investors avoid selling long-term holdings if they need money during a downturn. But more importantly, it gives investors flexibility to buy quality companies at a discount and hold them over the long run.

    Plus, instead of trying to time the exact bottom, investors can invest gradually. This approach can help ease the pressure of making one huge investment decision at the wrong time.

    That stated, investors should be careful about using leverage as a shortcut to protect their portfolios or profit from a potential market reversal. In fact, if the market moves against investors, these investments can rapidly see losses accelerate.

    Another way to manage risk is to spread it across different companies.

    Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a powerful driver of recent market rallies. However, these rallies have been concentrated in a few of the world's biggest companies. That alone creates potential risks.

    Industry observers note that specifically, if investor expectations around AI spending reset lower, valuations could take a bigger hit than the broad market might. Still, for investors, the takeaway isn't necessarily to abandon high-growth tech stocks. Instead, it's to avoid having an entire portfolio depend on a single name or theme.

    Investors might consider spreading their exposure across less correlated sectors such as healthcare, consumer staples, and financials. After all, these businesses have different economic drivers, which can help reduce the impact of weakness in any single industry.

    It has been revealed that additionally, it's worth looking beyond individual stocks. Broad-market exchange-traded funds (ETFs), for example, can provide exposure to companies across multiple industries, while bond funds and cash equivalents can add additional diversification. Doing so can help reduce portfolio volatility and limit the losses from any single investment.

    That brings us to another important consideration: the quality of companies investors actually own.

    Sources indicate that when economic conditions worsen, companies with high debt, weak cash flow, and limited pricing power can find themselves under pressure. On the other hand, businesses with healthy balance sheets, strong competitive advantages, and recurring revenue may be better positioned.

    That's why investors should review a company's fundamentals before deciding whether to invest.

    According to recent reports, specifically, long-term investors should look for companies that generate consistent free cash flow (FCF), maintain manageable debt levels, and have business models that can survive economic downturns. For example, companies selling essential products and services are likely to be more resilient when households reduce their spending.

    It has been revealed that that doesn't mean investors should automatically favor defensive stocks over growth companies. In fact, some long-term opportunities can still come from tech, industrials, and other high-growth industries. Ultimately, investors simply need to distinguish between companies benefiting from sustainable demand and those that rely mainly on hype.

    Of course, there's no guarantee that financially sound companies will avoid losses during a bear market, but focusing on the fundamentals gives investors a better starting point for finding companies worth holding through market volatility.

    Nobody knows for sure when the next bear market will come, but investors can already start preparing as early as today. In short, diversifying across sectors, prioritizing financially sound businesses, and maintaining cash reserves can help build a more resilient portfolio. Ultimately, the goal isn't to avoid every market decline, but to be in a stronger position when a bear market comes.

    By James Brumley – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:29AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    In a recent development, at first blush the suggestion is counterintuitive. A falling market is certainly nothing for investors to celebrate.

    As has been the case so often since taking the helm at Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%)(BRKB +0.37%) back in 1970, however, this bit of advice first dished out by Warren Buffett in his 1997 letter to Berkshire shareholders was eventually vindicated.

    In a recent development, granted, it was three years too early. The tech-driven rally underway at the time carried on and even accelerated into the early 2000s. That's when it all unraveled. From that year's peak to 2002's trough, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) fell on the order of 40%. Then five years following that multiyear low, the index had reclaimed everything it lost, rewarding those investors with enough forethought to celebrate the opportunity by diving into beaten-down stocks.

    It certainly wasn't the first time something like this had happened either.

    In a recent development, the irony? By the time the S&P 500 had doubled its 2002 low by mid-2007, the next cyclical headwind -- led by the subprime mortgage meltdown -- was already underway. Less than two years later, the index had lost a little more than half of 2007's peak value. And once again it was destined for a major recovery. Only this time, the S&P 500 would only need four years to recover, and would ultimately go on to quadruple its 2009 low before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic finally brought the rally to a screeching halt in early 2000.

    Industry observers note that even then, though, the pandemic-prompted bear market that pulled the S&P 500 down by one-third of its value would erase that loss before the end of the same year, en route to what would be a bull market worth 90% in less than two years. The 2022 bear market also dialed the index back by more than 20%, but the bull market since then is up more than 100% from the late-2022 bottom.

    The point is, every major and minor setback the stock market has suffered so far has eventually been recouped, and then surpassed.

    According to recent reports, it's not like Buffett doesn't take his own advice either. He famously bought a stake in then-deeply-discounted Goldman Sachs back in 2008, and locked in a 60% gain on this position in 2020. Berkshire added a bunch of now-privately-held construction materials companies between 2000 and 2002 as well, positioning it for a couple of waves of housing booms that would materialize in the meantime.

    It has been revealed that the point is, while corrections and bear markets feel pretty miserable at the time they're happening, Warren Buffett is right -- they're a reason to rejoice, particularly if you missed out on most of the bull market that preceded them. Dips are a second chance to step in at a discounted price regardless of how big or small they are.

    Industry observers note that just don't get too cheeky or clever when this window of opportunity opens. No one knows exactly when or where a bottom is going to be made, and plenty of investors have missed out because they were holding out for slightly better prices that never materialized. Any decent dip that offers an entry price you can live with in the long run is more than good enough.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
    • According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
    • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

    According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

    Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

    There are four main types of grants:.

    Federal grants come from the federal government.

    State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

    Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

    Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

    To receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

    Sources indicate that federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

    Some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

    In a recent development, after you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

    According to recent reports, most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal initiative.

    In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

    If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

    Grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

    Some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

    Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

    After your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment aims, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

    To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

    Your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

    Industry observers note that yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

    You don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

    If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

    You withdrew from your program.

    You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

    It depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

    If you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

    Grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.
