    Investing $500 a Month in Coca-Cola, Realty Income, and Altria Could Generate Over $1,000 in Monthly Dividend Income by 2046

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, will you need dividend income at some point in the future?
    • That isn't necessarily the only way to meet your future income needs, though.
    • And while nobody can perfectly predict the future, your most promising dividend prospects for this purpose are Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%), Realty Income (O +1.18%), and Altria Group (MO +1.95%).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 26, 2026 at 9:31AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    In a recent development, will you need dividend income at some point in the future? For most people who blueprint on eventually retiring from the world of work, the answer is yes. They're growing their nest eggs in the meantime, in fact, largely with the intention of converting their growth investments into income investments when the time comes.

    That isn't necessarily the only way to meet your future income needs, though. As difficult as it may be to believe, there's an argument to be made for beginning to build your dividend-paying positions right now, even if you don't need the income yet.

    And while nobody can perfectly predict the future, your most promising dividend prospects for this purpose are Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%), Realty Income (O +1.18%), and Altria Group (MO +1.95%).

    These names are among the market's most reliable and highest-yielding dividend payers, and each has raised its annualized dividend for at least 50 consecutive years, reflecting the resiliency of their underlying businesses. That makes all three of them Dividend Kings.

    Recent findings suggest that their dividend pedigrees aren't as crucial as the process, however. How does one turn a $500 monthly investment in these names into a portfolio capable of producing more than $1,000 in monthly dividend income by, say, 20 years from now, in 2046?

    There are two stages to the process.

    Industry observers note that the first is the growth phase. Rather than pocketing the dividends these stocks will be paying in the coming two decades, you'll be reinvesting these payments into more shares of the ticker while also purchasing more of these same stocks with your monthly contributions of $500.

    This is no minor growth driver. Over the past 20 years, dividend reinvestment has essentially doubled the effective net returns each of these stocks would have achieved with price appreciation alone.

    The other aspect of the first stage is a bit trickier to get a handle on. That's figuring out the likely net returns these three names will achieve between now and 2046. Although past performance doesn't guarantee future results, experienced investors know that it's a pretty good indicator of what's likely to happen.

    Sources indicate that nevertheless, given the modest but steady traction the smoking-cessation movement is getting, it seems unlikely that tobacco giant Altria will deliver a repeat performance of the past two decades in the next two. For that matter, Coca-Cola's net gains since 2006 have also been exaggerated.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that so, for the sake of simplicity and plausibility, let's just assume all three of these stocks have and will continue to at least match the overall market's average annual net gain of 10%. (Each has beaten this figure, actually.) Investing $500 per month in any instruments achieving this sort of annual return for 20 years would leave you with a portfolio worth a little more than $380,000 at the end of this time frame.

    According to recent reports, and again, just for the sake of simplicity, let's assume this $380,000 nest egg is evenly allocated between Altria, Realty Income, and Coca-Cola. Those are positions of roughly $127,000 each. How much dividend income would these collective investments be producing then?

    We're still required to make some assumptions, albeit not unreasonable ones. Namely, let's assume these stocks' current dividend yields will more or less be their yields at that time. That's 2.2% for Coca-Cola, 5.6% for Realty Income, and 6% for Altria. Based on those numbers, this $380,000 in stock holdings should generate over $17,000 in dividends every year, or more than $1,400 in monthly spendable income.

    In a recent development, just don't forget to turn your dividend reinvestment plan off when you're ready to start collecting these dividend payments in cash. That's the second stage of the process.

    These results are just hypothetical, of course, although the assumptions are rooted in real-world numbers that should be roughly repeatable.

    The big takeaway isn't identifying these three dividend payers as your top future income prospects, although there's little doubt that these companies will still be experiencing solid demand for their goods and services into the foreseeable future.

    It has been revealed that no, the real takeaway is just how much even small regular investments in dividend stocks, paired with a dividend reinvestment proposal, can grow your portfolio over time. This strategy can yield growth-like returns — the key is just giving it enough time to do the job. Note that most of the net growth for all three of these positions materialized in just the last one-third of the 20-year accumulation period.

    The other related takeaway is that even though it may be years down the road for you, it wouldn't be wrong to start thinking about — and even building — positions in the dividend-paying stocks that you know you'll want to own as your income-generating positions then. Although dividends paid by stocks not held in retirement accounts are taxable as income for the year in which they're paid, that may still be a smarter option for you than buying growth investments that will result in large capital gains tax bills when you're ready to convert them into income-generating holdings.

    Breaking: OMS Energy (OMSE) Q2 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3227 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 26, 2026 at 9:53AM EST.
    • Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst?
    • OMS Energy (OMSE +6.67%) reported a decrease in revenue for the first half of fiscal year 2027 but expanded its gross margin while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet with record cash reserves.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 26, 2026 at 9:53AM EST.

    Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

    OMS Energy (OMSE +6.67%) reported a decrease in revenue for the first half of fiscal year 2027 but expanded its gross margin while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet with record cash reserves. Management attributed the revenue decline primarily to procurement delays in Saudi Arabia, where orders under a long-term supply agreement are being deferred instead of canceled. The firm is actively diversifying its geographic footprint with fresh orders in Malaysia, Kuwait, and Pakistan while shifting toward a higher-margin services revenue mix. Strategic efforts focus on cost discipline and cash generation to manage through extended customer decision cycles.

    In a recent development, operator: Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining OMS Energy Technologies, Inc.'s Earnings Presentation for the first half of fiscal year 2027. Today's presentation is being recorded. The tech giant's financial and operating results for the 6 months ended September 30, 2026, have been released and are available on the OMS Investor Relations website at ir.omsos.com. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements typically contain words such as may, will, expect, target, estimate, intend, believe, potential, continue, or similar expressions. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected or anticipated.

    These include changes in customer spending and procurement, the timing of call-off orders and deliveries, geopolitical developments, supply chain conditions, and foreign exchange movements. Further information about risks is included in the organization's filings with the SEC. The company does not undertake any obligation to update forward-looking information, except as required under applicable law. Today's discussion also includes adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow, which are supplemental non-IFRS measures. Their definitions and reconciliations to the most directly comparable IFRS measures are included in the earnings release. I will now turn the presentation over to Mr. Meng Hock How. Please go ahead.

    Meng Hock How: Thank you, operator, and thank you to everyone joining us today. I am Meng Hock How, CEO of OMS Energy Technologies. I'll discuss our first half performance, what we're seeing in customer orders and the progress we're making across our business. I will then address several questions that we expect investors to have about the results. For investors newer to OMS, we are Singapore headquartered equipment manufacturer and engineered solutions supplier serving upstream oil and gas operators. Our core products include Surface Wellhead and Christmas Tree Systems, Specialty Connectors and Pipe. We also provide premium threading, repair, and other engineering services through 11 manufacturing facilities across 6 markets in Asia Pacific, Middle East, and North Africa. Turning to our results.

    Industry observers note that I'm pleased to report that we expanded our gross margin, generated strong cash flow and further strengthened our debt-free balance sheet in the first half. Gross margin increased to 31.4% from 28.2% in the prior year period, and net profit margin improved to 18.8% from 17.6%. We generated $25.3 million in operating cash flow and approximately twice our net profit and ended September with a record $172.3 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash or approximately $4.06 per share. We delivered these results while macro conditions remain challenging given ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain disruption in our major markets. Our facilities remained operational throughout the period.

    According to recent reports, customers continued to tender and place orders with OMS during the half, but took longer to commit and schedule deliveries, weighing on revenue. First half revenue was $66.7 million compared with $82.8 million a year ago, largely due to the slower pace of Saudi Aramco call-off orders. This was partially offset by increased activity in Malaysia and Thailand, showing the value of our diversified footprint. In the current environment, the challenge for OMS lies not in lack of opportunities, but in reduced visibility, extended decision cycle and execution timing. You will see that pattern throughout this period's result.

    With order timing harder to predict, we are concentrating on factors that we can control, including careful management of inventory, costs, and customer deliveries. By keeping inventory, purchasing and costs in line with the orders we actually received, we were able to protect profitability and generate strong cash flow despite fluctuating order volumes. Saudi Arabia is where reduced visibility and order timing have affected us most. Revenue from Specialty Connectors and Pipe was $37.1 million compared with $51.1 million a year ago as the timing of the order placed under our long-term supply agreement with Saudi Aramco continued to slow. I would like to emphasize, as previously mentioned, that these are deferred orders, not lost orders.

    Our agreement with Saudi Aramco remains intact. Our relationship remains strong, and there has been no cancellation. To that end, we continue to receive business from Aramco. In September, we declared a $7.1 million order for specialty connectors and pipe won through an open tender outside our long-term agreement. Since that award, we have received a call-off order of approximately $3 million under the long-term agreement as well as a separate $500,000 order for loose connectors for Aramco's float equipment. We view these awards as a reflection of Aramco's confidence in our product and the delivery record we have built in the Kingdom over 15 years.

    In a recent development, in Indonesia, our operation in Bogor just received an order for specialty pipe and connectors valued at approximately $396,000 for Pertamina North West Java. This is a follow-on from the order we announced in January 2026. Furthermore, our operations in Singapore and Malaysia secured their first order for specialty connectors and pipe for Petronas in Malaysia, valued at approximately $687,000. Of that amount, $367,000 was delivered during the first half of fiscal 2027. We also continue to bid for supply contracts with Kuwait Oil Tech giant, KOC, and are actively engaged in the tender process we have entered after we qualified for the approved vendor list in July.

    Recent findings suggest that also following that qualification, we received a $458,000 order from Tenaris for OMS connectors that we welded onto Tenaris pipe and supplied to Kuwait Oil Firm as part of Tenaris OCTG package. While modest in size, the Petronas and Tenaris order extend our specialty connectors and pipe business to 2 more national oil companies, which we believe can lead to additional business over time. We've also recently bid to supply specialty connectors and Pipe for a development in the South China Sea with results expected next month. If we are successful, this will mark our reentry into China after more than 10 years and represent further progress in our ongoing geographic diversification efforts.

    In a recent development, in surface wellhead and Christmas trees, we continue to win orders while revenue follows customer and project schedules. First half revenue from Surface Wellhead and Christmas Tree was $3.5 million compared to $6.2 million a year ago. Indonesia is the main market for this business and upstream activities there has been slow over the past year as newly introduced oil and gas projects have taken longer to come online. In September, we announced $2.3 million order from Pertamina Hulu Rokan under our existing 3-year supply contract following the contract extension we announced in March. We also recently received $766,000 order from Pertamina for choke valves, a component of Christmas tree systems.

    Separately, we are awaiting a call-off of approximately $1 million from Pertamina under an existing contract. We also completed the stackup and function test of a upcoming compact surface wellhead and Christmas tree system for Pertamina, a milestone in developing our wellhead product offering with an established customer. The equipment has been delivered and is being installed by Pertamina on its Tamadun-001 field, where it is carrying out an unconventional drilling program. Indonesia holds vast unconventional oil and gas resources, including shale gas, coal-bed methane, methane hydrate, and shale oil, and commercial development is still at an early stage. We believe this installation position us well as that activity develops.

    It has been revealed that OMS Singapore has also just delivered a complete 10,000 psi wellhead and Christmas tree system to Orient Petroleum in Pakistan, marking OMS Singapore's first delivery of such a system to the country. Orient Petroleum is one of Pakistan's largest private exploration and production company and has been operating since 1979. OMS Singapore has also received a supply contract for 2 sets of production tree for a Bleiswijk geothermal cluster in Netherlands. While the value is small at approximately $130,000, it is a step into the European energy sector that we want to build on. Across our service businesses, customers also continued to place orders during the half.

    Recent findings suggest that other ancillary services revenue rose to $9.4 million from $7.5 million, an increase of approximately 25%, supported by repair, refurbishment, and engineering work in Thailand and Malaysia. This maintenance work depends less on newly introduced project approval than equipment sales do. Premium threading services revenue was $16.7 million compared to $18 million. Together, our services business accounted for approximately 39% of first half revenue, up from approximately 31% a year ago. In Singapore, we've also secured an approximately $0.55 million of repair work on production risers for a large oilfield services company for the upcoming Kikeh 3B Phase 2 subsea project in Malaysia. The Kikeh field is operated by PTTEP Malaysia. Our backlog reflects the period's slower order timing pattern.

    It has been revealed that at September 30, it stood at $40.9 million compared to $60.7 million at March 31, primarily due to call-off timing under the Saudi agreement. Our backlog comprises confirmed orders that have not yet been recognized as revenue and are expected to be delivered within the following 12 months. It does not include orders received after September 30, including the additional Saudi Aramco order I mentioned earlier. A framework agreement, a tender opportunity, and a confirmed call-off each represent different stages of the customer's procurement process and the backlog captures only the last of those stages. Today, opportunities are taking longer to move from tender to award and from framework agreement to call-off.

    It has been revealed that to put the backlog figure in context, Saudi Aramco maintained its 2026 capital spending guidance of $50 billion to $55 billion when it reported third quarter's results this month. Aramco attributed lower upstream spending in the quarter, mainly to the timing of crude oil increment projects and several of its major upstream developments, including the Dammam development and the second phase of Jafurah are scheduled to come on stream in 2027. Across the wider region, BMI expects oil and gas capital spending to grow about 4% this year and to average approximately 6% a year from 2027 to 2030. Now let me walk through our financial results in more detail.

    First half revenue was $66.7 million compared to $82.8 million in the prior year period. Gross profit was $21 million compared to $23.3 million. Gross margin increased from 28.2% to 31.4%, supported by a more favorable mix in Saudi Specialty connectors and pipe and a greater contribution from higher-margin ancillary services in Thailand. Selling and general and administrative expenses were $7.1 million compared to $5.4 million in the prior year period. The increase primarily reflected personnel costs and professional services, governance, and compliance-related fees. Operating profit was $13.9 million compared to $17.9 million, and operating margin was 20.8% compared to 21.6%. Finance income increased to $2.4 million from $1.6 million, reflecting more cash placed in interest-earning deposits.

    Recent findings suggest that income tax expense was $3.6 million compared with $4.6 million, and our effective tax rate was 22.3% compared to 24%. Net profit was $12.6 million compared with $14.6 million, and net profit margin increased to 18.8% from 17.6%. Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.28 compared with $0.33, reflecting lower profit attributable to shareholders and a higher weighted average share count. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million compared to $21.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin held relatively steady at 25.9% compared with 26.4% despite the 19% decline in revenue. We continue to use this supplement measure alongside the IFRS results. The earnings release sets out the adjustment and the reconciliation from net profit. Cash generation remained an area of strength.

    Operating cash flow was $25.3 million compared with $26.4 million. Adjusted free cash flow was $19.9 million compared with $25.4 million. As described in our earnings release, this measure now deducts cash placed in fixed rate structured deposits, and the change from last year mainly reflects the $5 million we placed in these deposits during the period. Part of our cash generation came from a reduction in inventory, which contributed $9.5 million to operating cash flow compared to $12.2 million a year ago. Inventory ended September at $7.7 million compared to $17.2 million at March 31. The level of inventory and the timing of replenishment will affect cash flow as order activity changes.

    Industry observers note that we will continue to manage purchasing and production against the equipment needed for customer deliveries. Net cash used in investing activities was $5.4 million. This included $5 million placed in fixed rate structured deposits and approximately $0.4 million for property, plant, and equipment and software. These deposits are not included in our reported cash balance of $172.3 million. Cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash increased to a record $172.3 million at September 30 compared with $104.3 million at March 31. Our balance sheet remains free of bank borrowings. We continue to refine our capital allocation plan and assess investment opportunities while maintaining the financial flexibility to meet delivery commitments.

    Sources indicate that looking ahead, our immediate planning reflects the slow pace of Saudi call-off and the orders we have in hand across the business. The September Aramco tender win and the Pertamina order were declared with expected delivery dates in January and March 2027, respectively. We are focused on execution against the schedule and continued engagement with our customers. We remain cautious about the timing of a wider recovery in procurement. At the same time, we are encouraged by our recent order activity, the growing contribution from our services business and the opportunities we are pursuing across the Middle East and Asia.

    According to recent reports, we have long-term agreement with leading national oil companies, 11 manufacturing facilities close to our customers and more than $172 million in cash with no debt. We believe this strength positions OMS well to capture future opportunities. Before we close, I would like to address questions investors are likely to have in the half, including how current visibility compares with the expectation that we discussed in June. Question one, how much of the earnings decline is attributable to geopolitical tensions and have projects been canceled? We have not observed material projects cancellation directly attributable to geopolitical development. The effect has been indirect primarily through longer customer decision cycle, deferred projects award and increased caution in customer capital spending decisions.

    For OMS, the main operating matter has been the slower pace of Saudi call-off orders. Some customers have taken longer to finalize investment decisions or have adjusted project time lines, and it is difficult to isolate a specific financial impact. Opportunities remain in place, but decision and awards are taking longer. We are actively pursuing work in Malaysia, Indonesia, the UAE, Kuwait and China. Question two, is demand weakening, particularly in the Middle East? We would characterize the environment as one of increased caution rather than broad-based demand weakness. Activity levels vary by customers and markets. Customers continue to evaluate opportunities and pursue strategic projects, although decision-making and approval processes have become more measured.

    In certain cases, this has translated into longer approval and procurement cycles. For OMS, that shows up as a slower Saudi call-off and a longer gap between tender and award. Several of the largest oilfield services have also pointed to the limited near-term visibility in the Middle East in their recent results. Even so, Saudi Aramco has maintained its 2026 capital spending guidance and has continued to award us business, including the $7.1 million tender award in September and additional orders since then. Our focus remains on supporting customers while adapting to changing market conditions. Third question, have supply chain disruption become a major concern? Supply chain conditions remain manageable, but less predictable than in previous period.

    We have experienced longer lead time and occasional logistic challenges affecting certain projects. Management continues to work closely with suppliers and customers to mitigate these impacts where possible. The fourth question, how are margins holding up? And can they be sustained? Well, first half gross margin increased to 31.4% from 28.2%, supported by the mix of equipment specification and services. Operating margin was 20.8%. We continue to manage procurement, project execution and operating costs carefully. Our priority is maintaining financial discipline while remaining competitive in the markets we serve. However, if activity slows further in the second half, margins could be affected. We will continue to manage costs carefully as conditions evolve.

    Sources indicate that question five, do we expect conditions to improve in the second half? Given the uncertain geopolitical and macroeconomic environment, we do not believe it will be appropriate to speculate on the timing or extent of any improvement. Customers continue to tender and place orders with OMS. Improvement depends on visibility returning and decision cycles shortening, and we do not control that timing. Continued uncertainty could further influence customer spending, project timing and supply chain performance. We continue to maintain long-standing customer relationships, technical capabilities and a diversified market presence. Management remains focused on factors within our control, including customer engagement, operational execution, cost management, and cash generation.

    Recent findings suggest that sixth question is, does the expectation of modest FY 2027 revenue growth discussed in June still hold? Well, in June, we expected fiscal 2027 revenue to be modestly above fiscal 2026, assuming no further material geopolitical disruption. Since then, the Saudi call-off activity has remained slow and the timing of a broader pickup remains uncertain. Given the first half revenue of $66.7 million and the continued slow pace of call-off, we no longer expect fiscal 2027 revenue to exceed fiscal 2026. We're not providing a specific range today, and we will revision investors as visibility on order timing improves. The last point or question 7, how do you plan to use your cash?

    Well, our priorities are consistent with what we shared in June. First, we are reinvesting in core businesses, including capacity, certification, and in-region capabilities that support our growth. Second, we continue to review bolt-on acquisition opportunities with discipline and our cash position allows us to pursue them without raising newly introduced capital or taking on debt. We do not presently have a dividend and buyback program in place, but our balance sheet gives us the flexibility to introduce one when timing and conditions are right. We continue to refine our capital allocation blueprint, and we'll revision investors as it develops. With this, we conclude our prepared remarks. Thank you very much for joining us today.

    Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you all for participating. You may now disconnect your lines. Thank you.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic (ANT +1.08%) made history last week when it went public in the largest initial public offering (IPO) ever.
    • According to recent reports, but things can change quickly in the stock market, and a year from now, Anthropic could be much higher -- or much lower.
    • The theory behind the bull case for Anthropic is that its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) model will be integrated into businesses everywhere.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:13AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic (ANT +1.08%) made history last week when it went public in the largest initial public offering (IPO) ever. But so far, the stock isn't moving in the direction shareholders would hope for. The stock, which went public at $83 per share, opened its first day of trading at $111.50, and closed it at $97.17, has fallen to $77.40 as of this writing. That’s a 7% drop from the IPO price, and a much steeper one from the prices that retail investors could get on Day 1.

    According to recent reports, but things can change quickly in the stock market, and a year from now, Anthropic could be much higher -- or much lower. Let's consider what a $5,000 investment in Anthropic stock might be worth in a year.

    The theory behind the bull case for Anthropic is that its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) model will be integrated into businesses everywhere. As of now, it already has 11,900 customers paying it at least $100,000 annually, including 250 customers with annual spending of more than $10 million. Widespread enterprise adoption of Claude could lead to a state where it's simply viewed as a necessary part of business operations; that would generate incredible growth at Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, the manufacturer’s most recent results have been phenomenal. Trailing-12-month revenue increased 1,200% year over year in the third quarter, and if it continues to demonstrate such staggering growth, it could promptly become one of the largest companies in the world by sales. It would also become profitable at scale, and its vast investments in compute power — which it has been gobbling up from a roster of top AI infrastructure providers such as Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%)(GOOGL -2.13%), and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%)— would yield results. It has spending agreements with these companies and others to the tune of around $900 billion, with deals extending into 2036.

    Management sees vast use cases for its technology. It envisions AI helping to end poverty and cure disease as well as drive economic growth.

    Recent findings suggest that AI is definitely heating up, but it may not offer long-term growth in quite the way Anthropic imagines. To begin with, there are already many competitors offering foundation models, and as the technology changes, there could be more. The market is already forgetting how AI stocks tumbled when the Chinese-developed model Deepseek came onto the scene last year. There's no reason to believe other things like that can't happen. Anthropic itself is an extremely young company, and it only introduced Claude in 2023, pulling market share from OpenAI's ChatGPT.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, IPO stocks tend to have bumpy rides early on, and given Anthropic's high price-to-sales multiple of 29, the stock has considerable room to drop if the tech giant’s growth slows down. Wall Street expects its revenue to increase by 137% in 2027 — but that would be a major deceleration. If that forecast proves accurate, the market may conclude that Anthropic isn’t worth such a lofty sales multiple. If its top-line growth meets Wall Street's expectations, revenue would be about $83 billion. But if its P/S ratio gets cut in half to 14, its market cap would be $1.16 trillion. That's a 16% increase from today's value, turning a $5,000 investment made now into a position worth about $5,800.

    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1125 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the organization's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the organization as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    In a recent development, barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks latest CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that the case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    Industry observers note that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most crucial ideas.

    Industry observers note that WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Recent findings suggest that two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    Sources indicate that and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that indicates it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    #132026. Industry News: Rocket Lab Stock Just Fell to Its Lowest Price in About a Year. Is It a Buy Now?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (836 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Rocket Lab Stock Just Fell to Its Lowest Price in About a Year. Is It a Buy Now?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that rocket Lab (RKLB +2.26%) stock fell about 7% on Wednesday, Nov.
    • The growth stock had closed above $66 just two weeks before, soon after Rocket Lab's third-quarter results, and about a third of that value has vanished since.
    • But the business behind the stock is far bigger than it was the last time shares traded this low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:23AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Recent findings suggest that rocket Lab (RKLB +2.26%) stock fell about 7% on Wednesday, Nov. 25, to roughly $43 as I write. The drop left shares at their lowest price since early December 2025 and over 70% below their May 27 record close of $150.23.

    The growth stock had closed above $66 just two weeks before, soon after Rocket Lab's third-quarter results, and about a third of that value has vanished since.

    But the business behind the stock is far bigger than it was the last time shares traded this low. What hasn't changed is that Neutron, the reusable rocket behind Rocket Lab's long-term growth intends, hasn't yet flown.

    Recent findings suggest that the last time Rocket Lab stock traded this low, in early December 2025, the company's revenue for the previous four quarters came to around $555 million. For the last four quarters, it's about $882 million, almost 60% more. Growth has sped up, too. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 climbed 73% from a year earlier to a record $268 million, after growing 36% in the fourth quarter of 2025. And management expects fourth-quarter revenue of $270 million to $290 million, which at the midpoint would be 56% above the year-ago quarter -- still fast, though slower than the third quarter's rate.

    Sources indicate that the share count grew, too, but far more slowly. Rocket Lab sold around $3.9 billion in upcoming stock through September, partly to pay for its pending purchase of satellite operator Iridium Communications. Counting preferred stock that converts to common shares, it had about 15% more shares at the end of September than at the end of 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that that leaves much more revenue behind each share. At roughly $43, Rocket Lab is valued at about $29 billion, which comes to 33 times the revenue it took in over the last year. At the same share price in early December 2025, the stock traded at more than 40 times sales.

    Still, 33 times sales is a high valuation for a business that isn't profitable yet, and I think much of that price depends on Neutron.

    Rocket Lab now has 16 Neutron missions booked before the rocket's first flight, and half of them were signed in the third quarter alone, for over $515 million.

    Industry observers note that but at least six of those eight new missions aren't scheduled until late 2028 or later. Radar-satellite company ICEYE's three debuts start in late 2028, Muon Space's two are set for 2029 and 2030, and Starcloud's is booked for 2029.

    In a recent development, rocket Lab expects only around a third of its $3.6 billion total backlog (signed work it hasn't yet counted as revenue) to become revenue within 12 months. Neutron's far-off missions likely make up a big part of the rest.

    Sources indicate that neutron's first launch, meanwhile, is expected in 2027. Before Rocket Lab picks a specific date, it still needs to put together the rocket's first-stage tank and finish pressure and cryogenic (super-cold) testing, according to its last quarterly report.

    Recent findings suggest that neutron has to fly first, and even then its early missions might not make money. In the third quarter, Rocket Lab recorded a forward loss reserve (an expected loss booked ahead of time) on the vehicle for Neutron's second flight, because the rocket is still so early in development.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Until Neutron flies regularly, the losses will likely keep coming. Rocket Lab lost $18 million in the third quarter on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis, measured by earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA). That was smaller than its $26 million loss a year earlier, and management expects another loss of $14 million to $20 million in the fourth quarter.

    On the third-quarter earnings call, CFO Adam Spice mentioned capital spending should stay high as Neutron heads toward production, but he expects adjusted EBITDA to go positive within six months of the rocket's first successful test flight.

    In a recent development, I think it can be, for investors willing to wait for Neutron. Each share now comes with much more revenue than it did at this price a year ago, and customers keep booking Neutron debuts. But Neutron still has to show it can fly, then fly often. And a stock that shed a third of its value over two weeks might swing just as hard again. I'd consider buying in stages instead of all at once.

At the moment, 14% of the fund's assets are tied to Anthropic, according to the organization's website.Options volume on the fund jumped to more than 10x the 30-day average Monday, according to Cboe LiveVol data. Of the 42,300 contracts traded by midday, 41,800 were calls, with just 141 puts likely opened by buyers.

    According to recent reports, just shy of $5.5 million in options premium on DXYZ traded on Monday, with almost all of it tied to calls, but just marginally more spent buying than selling calls, according to SpotGamma. The highest-volume contract is currently the 30-strike call expiring Friday, a 90-cent contract that needs the fund to rally 19% into the weekend to pay off.Traders may want to be wary of how the fund traded around the SpaceX IPO: DXYZ surged almost 150% in May before unwinding all the gains in the weeks ahead of SpaceX's debut. Since then, the fund has barely moved, trading around $26.There are other bullish signs surrounding Anthropic's IPO in the derivatives markets. Current prices for perpetual futures on the blockchain exchange Hyperliquid are implying an opening price of $98, a big pop from the $70-$78 price range quoted in the firm's amended S1 filing.     • On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:28AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nano-X Imaging ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 25, 2026, Nano-X Imaging (NNOX -12.28%) confirmed revenue of $4.4 million. Management is pivoting from a medical-screening-as-a-service (MSaaS) pay-per-scan model to upfront equipment sales to accelerate cash generation. Investors must weigh whether commercial execution can catch up with technological development before cash reserves run thin. Three things management noted on the call stand out.

    In a recent development, nano-X is shifting away from its medical-screening-as-a-service (MSaaS) pay-per-scan contract model toward capital expenditure (CapEx) upfront sales to bolster cash flow immediately. Commercial adoption has lagged technological development, forcing management to prioritize near-term liquidity.

    Sources indicate that the company opened its first Nanox Imaging Network (NIN) location in Philadelphia, establishing an operational benchmark for specialized clinical deployments. Management expects each network facility to generate recurring revenue through higher reimbursement rates in dedicated care segments.

    With cash reserves standing at $26.6 million as of Sept. 30, 2026, Nano-X is cutting operating expenses (OpEx) to extend its financial runway. Management is restructuring international operations and moving chip production to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners to reduce costs.

    Commercial execution remains the core focus as Nano-X works to convert technical recognition into sustainable revenue. Proprietary digital 3D imaging technology, expanding distribution partnerships, and growing artificial intelligence (AI) software integrations provide structural advantages for future growth. Management is watching channel partner sales performance, system installation timelines, and operating expense reductions.

    Financial flexibility and disciplined execution will determine whether the business achieves long-term commercial viability.

    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Worried About a Market Crash? 2 Gold Mining Stocks to Buy Before 2026 Ends.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (730 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Agnico Eagle Mines ›.
    • According to recent reports, if you're building a portfolio to survive a potential market crash or economic downturn, Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM +3.03%) and Franco-Nevada (FNV +3.06%) should be on your list.
    • All gold mining stocks present a relatively high level of risk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Halley – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Agnico Eagle Mines ›.

    According to recent reports, if you're building a portfolio to survive a potential market crash or economic downturn, Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM +3.03%) and Franco-Nevada (FNV +3.06%) should be on your list. The Toronto-based companies combine exposure to gold, a traditional safe-haven asset, with strong balance sheets that can withstand liquidity crunches.

    All gold mining stocks present a relatively high level of risk. The price of gold vacillates wildly. The precious metal hit an all-time high of $5,589.38 per ounce at the end of January but is now trading at around $3,572 per ounce.

    It's cost-intensive to run a mining company, and even when gold prices are rising, operational costs and debt loads can easily outweigh a company's profit potential. Agnico Eagle Mines and Franco-Nevada both mitigate those risks, but in substantially different ways.

    In a recent development, agnico Eagle's gold mines present less jurisdictional risk from geopolitical and labor disruptions than typical gold mining stocks. The firm operates in Tier-1 mining-friendly locations, including Canada, Australia, Finland, and Mexico.

    Agnico also hasn't had to make expensive acquisitions of late thanks to continued underground expansion at its Canadian Malartic location and project growth at Hope Bay in Nunavut, Canada, and at Ikkari in Finland.

    According to recent reports, in the third quarter, the company reported nine-month all-in sustaining costs (AISC) of $1,529 per ounce of gold while selling each ounce for an average of $4,537. Agnico reported nine-month earnings per share (EPS) of $9.25, up 58% year over year. The stock is up more than 14% so far this year, and even with that gain, the stock is trading at below 13 times earnings.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that the organization also raised its dividend by 12.5% this year to $0.45 per share quarterly, yielding around 1.11% at its current share price, which is right around the S&P 500 average. The cash dividend payout ratio is only 19.3%, so it is more than well-covered.

    In a recent development, franco-Nevada is a gold streaming tech giant. It doesn't actually mine for gold but earns royalties from the gold-mining companies to which it has provided up-front funds. When gold prices rise, the company benefits either from royalty payments or the right to purchase a portion of the mine's gold production at a pre-agreed-upon discounted price, known as a stream.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that the company has interests in 445 assets, including 129 operating mines. Most of its money comes from gold mining, roughly 70%, though it also makes money from natural gas liquids, oil, gas, and silver.

    Because it only needs a handful of employees -- 44 full-time and five part-time contractors, as of the end of 2025 -- to operate, its margins are higher than typical mining companies.

    Sources indicate that through nine months, the firm reported EPS of $6.30, up 63.1% year over year, and record revenue of $1.78 billion, up 45% over the same period a year ago. Adjusted net income margin improved by 710 basis points to 65.8%. Even with those numbers, its shares have fallen more than 7% so far this year.

    Franco-Nevada's dividend yields 0.72% at its current share price. The firm has raised its quarterly dividend for 19 consecutive years, including a 16% hike this year to $0.44 per share. Like Agnico Eagle, its dividend is well-covered, with a cash dividend payout ratio of only 26.3%.

    Gold's price has been weighed down this year by high interest rates, as high-yield bonds have become a more attractive vehicle for passive investing. However, if the stock market declines sharply, rather than raising rates, the Federal Reserve would likely lower them, making gold more attractive.

    In the meantime, Agnico Eagle and Franco-Nevada are financially healthy and more stable than most mining stocks, with safe dividends.

    Though semiconductor stocks have taken a beating lately, a closer look at the financial performance of companies in this sector clearly indicates that the sell-off isn't justified.

    The semiconductor industry's revenue has been growing at an impressive pace, driven by rising demand for chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) applications, especially in data centers. This explains why the semiconductor industry's revenue in 2026 is anticipated to increase by 111% to $1.8 trillion, according to semiconductor intelligence provider TechInsights.

    What's more, TechInsights predicts that the industry's revenue will soar to $2.6 trillion next year. That's why now is a good time to take a closer look at a top semiconductor stock while it trades at an attractive valuation -- Lam Research (LRCX -5.68%) -- before it steps on the gas next year.

    Industry observers note that techInsights estimates that the memory market's revenue could hit $1.6 trillion next year, accounting for 61% of the overall semiconductor market. The firm adds that the memory market could clock higher revenue next year if there are no supply constraints.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that not surprisingly, memory manufacturers are ramping up capital expenditures. Micron Technology, for instance, is estimating $25 billion in capex for the first half of fiscal 2027, followed by higher spending in the second half. Micron spent $27.4 billion on capex in fiscal 2026, suggesting its spending could double this year.

    Given that memory supply conditions are expected to tighten in 2027 and 2028, according to Micron, and other memory manufacturers expect the shortage to last until 2030, I won't be surprised to see memory capex jump higher in the coming years. This is great news for Lam Research, a semiconductor equipment manufacturer that's benefiting from the memory shortage.

    Lam Research's revenue in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 shot up by 54% from the year-ago period. The tech giant reported non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.20, up 75% from the year-ago period. Investors should note that Lam Research gets 46% of its revenue from sales of memory manufacturing equipment, which explains the impressive growth in revenue and earnings. Specifically, Lam's revenue from sales of memory equipment increased by 120% year over year in the previous quarter.

    Sources indicate that even better, Lam's growth is poised to accelerate in the current quarter. The firm's $8.6 billion revenue estimate for the current quarter implies a 61% increase over the year-ago period. The adjusted EPS estimate of $2.33 would be an 83% improvement from the same quarter last year. As investments in memory manufacturing equipment increase in 2027 and beyond, Lam should be able to sustain its solid growth rate.

    It has been revealed that analysts are forecasting a 66% increase in its EPS in the current fiscal year (which ends in June next year). They are expecting healthy double-digit growth over the next two fiscal years as well, though don't be surprised to see it outperform those expectations due to the tight memory supply, which will encourage manufacturers to invest in more capital equipment.

    LRCX EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    In fact, Lam estimates that spending on wafer and fabrication equipment (WFE) could increase from the mid-$150 billion range this year to more than $200 billion in 2027. That implies a potential increase of almost 30%.

    Recent findings suggest that lam management noted on the recent earnings call that it has been gaining market share in the WFE space and sees opportunities for further share gains. So, there is a strong likelihood that Lam's growth will outpace analysts' expectations in 2027 and beyond.

    Lam Research stock has lost 53% of its value since the beginning of July. The stock trades at just 19 times forward earnings, only a slight premium to the S&P 500 index's forward earnings multiple of 18.

    We have already seen that Lam's EPS is on track to increase by 66% this year, well above the 34% growth that S&P 500 companies are expected to deliver. Analysts expect Lam to outperform the S&P 500's earnings growth next year as well. So, it is easy to see why this semiconductor stock is expected to soar by 89% over the coming year, based on the 12-month median price target of $350, according to CNN.

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (516 w)

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • In a recent development, implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    In a recent development, implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Sources indicate that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is at the moment 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    Recent findings suggest that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    S&P 500 Sell-Off: Here's Why I'm Not Panicking -- and What I'm Doing Instead

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn.
    • It has been revealed that as of Nov.
    • If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 26, 2026 at 10:45AM EST.

    Monday was a great example of why investors shouldn't panic sell during a correction or significant market downturn. On Nov. 23, the S&P 500 jumped nearly 5%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 3% and the Nasdaq Composite had one of its best days ever, rising 1,471 points, or 6.5%.

    It has been revealed that as of Nov. 20, the Nasdaq had been in near bear market territory, down 18% from its all-time high of 27,599 on Oct. 6. But on Nov. 23, with its nearly 1,500-point gain, it surged to 24,089. It is still down 12% from Oct. 6, and there may be volatile days ahead, but days like Monday are one reason you don't want to panic sell during a downturn.

    If you did sell shares in a Nasdaq or tech-focused ETF, or a stock like Nvidia, which gained some 30% on the day alone after CEO Jensen Huang was rehired, you would have lost out on a huge return.

    And it's just not a one-off type scenario that won't ever happen again. There are stats to show how much it can negatively impact your portfolio when you miss the market's best days during the correction of a bear market.

    Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

    Earlier this year, the Hartford Funds released a report that examined this very subject. It found that from 1950 through 2025, 76% of the market's best days were either during a bear market or within the first two months of a bull market. Of that, 48% came during a bear market. We're not yet in a bear market, but that could certainly change in the months ahead.

    According to recent reports, the Hartford report also compiled some numbers on how missing out on the best days would affect a long-term portfolio. It revealed that $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 in 1996 would grow to $192,167 after 30 years, through 2025, based on the average annual total returns of the S&P 500.

    If you missed the market's 10 best days, that would bring it down to $85,490. If you missed the best 20 days, the total would be $49,551. If you missed the market's best 30 days, you'd have $31,123 -- 84% less than if you stayed fully invested all 30 years.

    Fidelity did a similar study in August, putting a slightly finer point on it. It looks at the impact of missing the market's best days since 1988. A $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 from Jan. 1, 1988 to Dec. 31, 2025 would generate $616,013. Missing just the five best days would result in 38% less in your portfolio, about $380,479.

    There are a few things to understand that should help guide you through bear markets and rough patches.

    One, understand that bear markets do not last as long as bull markets, nor do they have a bigger net effect on your portfolio. A study by the Hartford Funds also found that there have been 27 bear markets since 1928 and 28 bull markets. The average length of a bear market is 289 days, while the average bull market lasts 988 days. Further, the Hartford Funds research indicated that stocks lose 35% on average in a bear market and gain 112% on average in a bull market.

    It has been revealed that two, over the past 30 years, the S&P 500 has averaged a 14.4% annualized total return, while the Nasdaq has averaged a 17.2% return. That's through the dot-com bust, the Great Recession, the COVID bear market, and the 2022 bear market. So, patience has been rewarded over the years.

    And three, downturns and bear markets are a great time to buy, not sell. Many good companies with strong fundamentals in market-leading positions get caught up in negative waves. When that happens, it is time to buy these great stocks at discounts.

    In general, downturns are an opportune time to review your holdings. While there may be great buys out there in a bear market, you may also see some stocks that are still overvalued, may be overleveraged, and may be facing industry or economic headwinds.

    The best thing to do is check their P/E ratios and valuation metrics, as well as their earnings outlooks. You may find the money invested in those stocks is put to better use in a broad ETF that tracks the Nasdaq or S&P 500 or one of the discount stocks you identified. This is how I approach downturns.

    Meta Platforms Just Partnered With Walmart. Here's Why Investors Should Pay Attention

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.
    • One vital debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the manufacturer's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified.
    • Recent findings suggest that that's a significant decline.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    One vital debate between Meta Platforms' (META +3.40%) bulls and bears is whether the manufacturer's massive artificial intelligence (AI) spending is justified. The bears certainly have a point: The tech leader's free cash flow is declining, largely due to capex spending tied to its AI build-out. In the third quarter, Meta posted negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.6 billion in the year-ago quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that that's a significant decline. However, Meta Platforms' AI-related initiatives are slowly taking shape, and a recent partnership with Walmart (WMT -0.28%) highlights the opportunity ahead for the organization.

    Recent findings suggest that first, let's back up a little. Meta Platforms released its Muse AI agent to the public in early September. It quickly became one of the most downloaded iOS apps. Meta later released several other versions of Muse, including one for small businesses. Management noted on the company's third-quarter earnings call that 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse within a month and a half of its release. The tech giant also said that 25% of those who had set up Muse used it daily, and growth remained strong.

    Recent findings suggest that but how does Meta plan to monetize Muse? The AI agent offers subscriptions for people who want higher usage capabilities (the base version is free). But Meta is targeting a potentially more lucrative opportunity. It plans to charge retailers transaction fees every time Muse helps a consumer make a purchase. That brings us to the company's partnership with Walmart. Meta Platforms and Walmart have partnered to integrate Muse with Walmart's e-commerce infrastructure through the retailer's Agent Gateway.

    It has been revealed that the integration allows consumers to use Muse to discover products, compare prices, find deals, and complete purchases on their behalf, subject to user-defined permissions and spending limits. While the precise financial details of this deal were not disclosed, Meta could earn commission fees for transactions Muse helps facilitate.

    Walmart is one of the largest retailers in the world, so this partnership is an important one for Meta. It could also help increase Muse's adoption. Some retailers are hesitant to get on board because they fear it will disrupt their business models and undermine their ability to protect customer relationships, as Meta's CFO, Susan Li, said.

    Industry observers note that this may happen if agents like Muse become the primary shopping interface -- instead of visiting a retailer's website, consumers could ask an agent to compare prices, quality, and other factors across many retailers, thereby potentially reducing retailers' direct relationships with consumers. Even so, consumers' adoption will largely determine where this market is headed.

    If Muse can continue gaining users, a significant percentage of them use the agent to make purchases, and at least some retailers start adapting to the change -- as Walmart is doing -- that could force other retailers to follow suit. Eventually, Meta could generate significant sales from transaction fees.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Of course, Meta's core advertising business remains healthy. In the third quarter, the company's revenue increased by 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. It also ended the period with 3.64 billion daily active people, an increase of 3% year over year. Meta's AI-powered algorithms across its websites and apps have helped grow engagement.

    As CEO Mark Zuckerberg pointed out, Facebook and Instagram are hitting near all-time highs in engagement, and Threads -- Meta's competitor to X (formerly Twitter) -- has overtaken X in monthly actives. The point is that even before we look at Meta's opportunity with Muse, the firm's underlying business looks strong. It's also worth noting that building the capacity required to support an agent like Muse requires substantial upfront investments.

    According to recent reports, meta is dishing out that money today, but the manufacturer's expenses in this area should decrease over time, and as Muse gains traction, revenue growth, profits, margins, and free cash flow could jump. Lastly, Meta is trading at 16.3x forward earnings, which, in my view, is more than fair, considering the company's robust underlying business and long-term opportunities in advertising and AI.

    Latest Update: AMD dives on short seller report of alleged China exposure

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (259 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".
    • Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
    • The report claims that "after the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the organization kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also stated that fresh export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson said in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "key" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.
